messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PROD ALERT 2230011223 - tokenizer-preproc group in us-west-2 showing repeated OOMKilled restarts. Paging oncall.
rafael: noticed a tight cluster of OOMKilled on preproc jobs. Heap profile shows runaway rss growth during tokenization of certain inputs.
nina: stack traces show tokenizer.normalize and regex cleanup running for minutes, memory grows linearly. Example problematic input pattern: repeated nested arrays and very long string fields (likely base64). No GPU/CUDA errors in node logs.
leo: customer impact: a few enterprise customers reported timeouts and incomplete generations. Rate of 5xxs peaked at 14% for the generation route for ~9 minutes.
infra-bot: node kernel message: "Out of memory: Killed process 3671 (python3)." Node is c5a.large-style CPU instance used for preproc.
rafael: quick mitigation proposal: 1) apply temporary API edge payload size cap (1MB), 2) enable lightweight early-reject heuristics for base64-like runs > 100k, 3) spin up extra cpu-preproc nodes, 4) bump preproc container memory limit from 1Gi -> 2Gi while we patch.
nina: pushing a Canary sanitizer that replaces long base64 with token placeholder and enforces a hard per-request tokenize timeout (2s). Deploying to 1/4 of preproc.
leo: applying edge cap now:

```
# block large payloads at edge
redwood-edge set-limit --route /v1/generate --max-body 1048576
```

infra-bot: autoscaling cpu-preproc pool +5 nodes. New nodes ready in ~60s. Observing lower queue depth.
rafael: canary sanitizer logs:
```
[10:03:12] sanitizer: replaced base64-run length=312345 with <BASE64_TRUNC>
[10:03:12] tokenizer: tokenization_time=0.72s tokens=12000
[10:03:12] route: directed to small-tokenizer
```
leo: one canary instance crashed with ValueError while trying to decode malformed base64. Rolling image with try/except to guard against decode errors.
nina: rolled fix. Canary stable, tokenization times for sanitized requests ~<1s. Overall CPU utilization on preproc pool reduced from 95% -> 62% after scale and sanitizer.
cs-bot: CS ticket #CS-4307 created for impacted customers. Initial mitigation note posted. Customers notified of partial degradation window 10:02-10:12 PDT.
rafael: root cause (prelim): API allowed extremely large or deeply nested inputs that trigger pathological regex/normalizer code paths in tokenizer, causing sustained memory growth and kernel OOM kills. Not an inference/GPU issue.
leo: severity: Sev-3. Channel will be kept open until stable handoff. Update cadence 10m.
oncall: preparing handoff note. Summary draft:
- incident start: 2230011223
- region: us-west-2
- symptoms: repeated preproc pod OOMKilled, increased 5xxs and latencies for generation endpoints
- immediate mitigations applied: edge payload cap, sanitizer truncation, memory bump on preproc, scaled cpu-preproc pool, rolling restart of faulty canary
- current status: stable, metrics normalized
- next steps & owners: add gateway cap + depth checks (infra, 24h); implement tokenizer timeouts + catch-all guards (nina, 72h); add fuzz tests for nested/base64 inputs (rafael, 72h); customer comms & RCA (support, 48h)

nina: adding follow-up: instrument tokenizer to emit "heavy-prompt" telemetry tag when inputs exceed heuristic (length, depth, base64 runs) so we can alert earlier.
rafael: will add a safe-mode tokenizer that rejects early if normalization loops exceed X iterations.
leo: leaving handoff. @oncall take it. I'll be reachable if needed.
oncall: taking over monitoring. Will watch for regressions and coordinate with infra if pods start flapping again. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident 2230011223 moved to MONITORING. Next auto-update in 30m or on events."
